uncertainties: EXPECTED_CORE_REACTIONS IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. This is a review of the sideroflexin (SLC56) gene family. It names heme biosynthesis repeatedly but does not state a single heme-biosynthesis transformation: no reaction in the file has both a substrate and a product named on the heme pathway. This is the correct curation, not a failure to look. I read the whole 67,304-character file; the body ends around character 24,000 and everything after the figure legends is references.

Verified by exhaustive substring search over full_text: 'succinyl' occurs 0 times; 'aminolevulinic' occurs exactly once (in the ALAS2 naming clause); 'protoporphyrin' occurs 0 times; 'porphyr' occurs 0 times. So ALAS2 is named with neither substrate nor product, and ferrochelatase is named with neither substrate nor product. Any reaction attributed to either would be imported from outside this paper.

S2 (the ferrochelatase step) is the weakest entry in this file and I would not defend it hard. The paper names ferrochelatase and places it inside heme biosynthesis by implication ('regulates heme biosynthesis by modulating ferrochelatase levels'), but it never calls it a stage and never says what it catalyses. A reviewer who deletes S2 is not obviously wrong. I kept it at low confidence because a named-but-undetailed branch is information the schema exists to record.

S1 is likewise a stage named only by function ('the rate-limiting step in heme biosynthesis'), not by chemistry. detailed_in_paper is false for both subprocesses; there is nothing in this paper that could make either true.

ALAS2 and ferrochelatase are recorded as important participants with reason 'distinguishes_identity_or_direction' rather than as reaction enzymes, because there is no reaction for them to be enzymes of. This is a slightly unusual use of the reason code and a reviewer should confirm it is the intended one; the alternative was to omit both, which would have lost the paper's only heme-pathway enzyme names.

CROSS-PAPER LEAKAGE RISK, stated explicitly: PMC12856317 (also assigned to me, also heme biosynthesis) DOES assert the ALAS2 condensation of glycine and succinyl-CoA. Nothing from that paper was carried into this one. The glycine entry here rests solely on this paper's own sentence 'Glycine is the direct precursor for heme'.

The paper fully specifies two reactions with both sides named — the SHMT2 serine-to-glycine cleavage and SFXN1 serine transport — and neither is heme biosynthesis. Both are in out_of_scope. They are the most plausible thing an extractor would wrongly retain as heme chemistry, because they are the only complete transformations in the file and glycine is their product.
